newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht unabashed by banking measures.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht unabashed by banking measures.

text.p: Southeast Asian regional currencies were generally weaker on Friday in the face of a resurgent U.S. dollar, which rallied to 113.65 yen from around 113 in early trade.
"The backdrop is of a stronger dollar," said a Singapore-based dealer with a large European bank.
The Thai baht was flat despite a raft of economic figures on Thursday afternoon and a new set of measures by the authorities aimed at propping up the beleaguered local banking sector.
The Bank of Thailand released data on Thursday showing Thai foreign resrves had fallen by $4 billion in May to $33.3 billion following large-scale intervention to support the baht.
It also said Thailand's trade deficit had widened to a 12-month high of 41.0 billion baht in April.
On Friday, the Thai stock exchange suspended trade in shares of nine finance firms pending their merger with other parties.
But dealers said offshore liquidity has fallen so sharply there was practically no foreign exchange market to react.
Most traders who still believed the baht would devalue had rolled their shorts forward to three-months.
"The crunch for them will come mid-August," said one dealer.
Almost all other speculative activity had disappeared.

"A week or two ago people could still exploit the yield curve, borrowing 12 months and selling one month, but even that is a dying trade," he said. "The central bank has successfully squeezed almost all the liquidity out of this market."
By 0330 GMT, spot offshore baht was steady around 25.32/42 to the dollar while the onshore baht was quoted at 25.85/90.
The Indonesian rupiah eased in slow trading in the face of the stronger dollar and on ample liquidity, dealers said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,430.50/31.50 by 0330 GMT against an opening of 2,430.00/30.75.
Dealers said the rupiah had suffered as the dollar rose against the yen but added that corporate demand appeared able to support rupiah around 2,431.50/.75 for the time being.
Resistance for the rupiah was seen around 2,430.50/.75.
Dealers in Jakarta said the rupiah firmed briefly at the opening on worries rupiah liquidity would remain tight following a jump in overnight rupiah call money late on Thursday.

"Operators had expected the rupiah liquidity to be tight after the overnight call money jumped to a high of 26 percent in late session yesterday from only 10 percent earlier," one foreign bank dealer said.
But the central bank's injection of 328 billion rupiah helped increase rupiah liquidity and ease the spot rate.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,425/2,617 and its conversion band also by one point to 2,425/2,473 on Thursday.
The Malaysian ringgit remained weak against the dollar, pressured by persistent dollar bids by offshore players.

"The market is still short (of the dollar) and dollar/ringgit should be trading a little bit higher," said a European bank dealer in Singapore. "But topside is again expected to be capped at 2.5240/50."
Dealers said the recent weakening of three-month interbank rates, which had fallen to around 7.40 percent from almost 8.00 percent two weeks ago, was gradually putting pressure on ringgit.

But dollar gains were still being capped by fears of central bank intervention. Although there had been no sign of Bank Negara's presence, dealers believed the central bank was monitoring the situation.
Dealers said the dollar/ringgit remained well supported at the 2.5200 level with buying interest seen from offshore centres as well as Kuala Lumpur.
Corporate demand for the mid-year book closing had been one of the key factors contributing to the dollar's strength.
By 0330 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5226/36 a dollar. It closed at 2.5207/17 in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
Across the Causeway in Singapore, the ringgit was quoted at 0.5650/56 Singapore dollar, down from 0.5657/63 in early trade.
One Singapore-based analyst said the Sing appeared to have gained a little from the ringgit's weakness but activity had been very low and the currency remained steady around 1.4260/70.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Chris Johnson in Singapore (65-8703199)
